title: Glucosinolate Accumulation Kinetics and Cold-Stress Induced Anthocyanin Biosynthesis in Brassica oleracea
author: Dr. vmffkxhs2362
abstract: Glucosinolates and anthocyanins contribute to the antioxidant capacity and bitter flavor profile of curly kale. We investigated temperature DIF (+8°C day/night differential) and sulfur fertigation ($SO_4^{2-}$ 65 ppm) on myrosinase enzyme activity and glucoraphanin accumulation. Cold night temperature (12°C) combined with 25% blue LED enrichment stimulated myrosinase kinetics, doubling total glucosinolate yield.
key_findings: Cold night treatment (12°C) increased glucoraphanin concentration by 112% compared to constant 20°C.
Myrosinase cleavage activity reached peak Vmax of 4.8 μmol/min/mg protein under 65 ppm sulfur fertigation.
Anthocyanin optical density at 530nm increased 2.4-fold, imparting deep purple leaf pigmentation.
